items.title: Karen Rathwell, Member Water Watchers and the Ontario Salt Pollution
notes: Coalition appeared before Council to outline the harmful effects of road salt, a toxic substance because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental damage. She asked Council to urge the Provincial government to take the following action:
1. Establish an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the best courses of action to protect freshwater’
2. Revamp limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard Best Management Practices;

3. Commit to the reduction of the use of road salt as much as possible while maintaining safety on roads, parking lots and sidewalks; and 4. Forward accepted resolution to all municipalities within the County, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Conservation Ontario, the Ontario Municipal Water Association, Minister Todd McCarthy (MECP), Attorney General Doug Downey, and Premier Doug Ford.

items.title: Ernest Kalwa, resident re Use of sidewalk and road salt appeared
notes: before Council suggesting the Township consider reducing the use of road salt and consider more environmentally and pet friendly alternatives that have been available for decades. He indicated the Township needs to recognize and immediately address the excessive use of road salt and sidewalk salt that is causing irreversible environmental damage to our rivers, the great lakes, and concrete infrastructure (bridges, buildings, steps, sidewalks, etc.). Mr. Kalwa requested Council adopt the draft resolution provided in the material submitted in order to support the need for Provincial action on salt pollution from road salt.
Councillor MacDonald read the following:

Whereas road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt;
and

Whereas salt levels in Ontario’s groundwater aquifers, creeks, rivers, and lakes have increasingly worsened since the 1970s, seriously affecting municipal drinking water sources and aquatic life; and Whereas the Township of Centre Wellington takes actions to minimize salt impacts, local salt concerns and economic damages from salt, etc., and

Whereas the Ontario and Canadian governments have taken many actions over the past 25 years including setting water quality guidelines, developing voluntary codes of practice, signing the Canada-Ontario Great Lakes Agreement, and holding workshops, yet still the salt problem continues to grow; and

Whereas numerous situation analyses have recommended salt solutions involving liability protection, contractor certification, government-approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) and salt management plans; and

Whereas increased numbers of slips and falls claims, and other injury/collision claims related to snow and ice, are resulting in salt applicators overusing salt beyond levels considered best practices; and Whereas unlimited contractor liability is making it difficult or expensive for snow and ice management contractors to obtain insurance coverage, resulting in contractors leaving the business, thereby making it difficult for municipalities and private owners to find contractors; and Whereas the Snow and Ice Management Sector (SMS) of Landscape Ontario is working with the Ontario government to institute a limited liability regime for snow and ice management, including enforceable contractor training/certification and government-approved BMPs for salt application; and
Whereas many Ontario municipalities have Salt Management Plans, but these often require updating in light of improved science and better salt management practices now available;
Whereas environmentally friendly and pet friendly alternatives to road salt and sidewalk have been widely available for decades and are used successfully world wide;
Therefore Be It Resolved That:

1. The Township of Centre Wellington urges the province of Ontario to work urgently with key stakeholders to develop limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard BMPs for snow and ice management;
and

2. The Township of Centre Wellington urges the province of Ontario to create and fund an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the province and municipalities on the best courses of action to protect freshwater ecosystems and drinking water from the impacts of salt pollution; and

3. The Township of Centre Wellington commits to the reduction of the use of road salt as much as possible while maintaining safety on roads, parking lots and sidewalks by immediately incorporating environmentally friendly and pet friendly alternatives to road salt and sidewalk salt; and 4. This resolution be sent to all municipalities within the County of Wellington, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Conservation Ontario, Minister Andrea Khanjin (MECP), Interim Minister Todd McCarthy (MECP), Attorney General Doug Downey, and Premier Doug Ford.
Councillor MacDonald suggested this matter and the proposed resolution be referred to staff for a report.

items.title: Parking By-law and Transition to AMPS
notes: Report from K. O'Kane, Managing Director of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk
K. O'Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk provided an overview of the new draft parking by-law and new Administrative Monetary Penalty By-law.

Staff responded to questions regarding improved signage, the timeframe and scope of the pavement marking program, extending the number of exemptions per household, overnight parking in municipal lots and additional accessible parking spaces.

Discussion ensued and Members of Council expressed a desire to provide exemptions for 4 registered vehicles per household and to provide overnight parking in identified lots within the downtown cores.

Councillor Lustgarten-Evoy requested consideration be given to extending the number of exemptions per household to 4 and Councillor Wilton requested an amendment to the parking by-law to permit parking overnight in municipal parking lots located at 160 Provost Lane, Menzies Lane, and 25 Metcalfe.
Mayor Watters called for a 7 minute recess and the meeting resumed.
